scope: Final O1 parsed-query-reuse candidate versus main, six paired TCP rounds and two descriptive UDP guard pairs. New code identity; not repeated selection of an unchanged artifact.

statistics.TCP: Six same-seed adjacent main/post pairs, three AB and three BA. Paired log-ratio t interval df5 for post/main; retain all per-round and relative-order values.

estimator.primary: measurement cgroup usage_usec delta / successful completions inside the measurement epoch
secondary: raw CPU total and busy fraction
estimator.estimate: geometric mean of six paired fix/main CPU ratios; 95% t interval on paired log ratios, df=5, t=2.570581835636305
estimator.diagnostic: all six pair values, median, AB/BA subgroup medians, and exact 64-sign-flip p on mean paired log ratio; p is descriptive only
decision: Lower 95% ratio bound >1: CPU cost increase confirmed for this Oracle workload, even if smaller than 10%.
Lower bound >1.10: increase above 10% confirmed; point estimate >1.10 without this bound retains magnitude uncertainty.
CI crossing 1 is unresolved, not proof of noise or no regression. Conflicting median/AB/BA groups require causal follow-up.
Upper bound <1.10 can bound this tested workload below the 10% scale, but cannot establish zero regression.
No W/range filter, no all-directions requirement, no pooling request samples as independent runs.
Intervals are per scenario and rely on paired log-ratio assumptions; not familywise confidence across three scenarios.
estimator.invalid_data: Never delete, retry, replace or select windows. Preserve behavior errors and method failures. Report all analyzable values; incomplete/invalid/generator-limited scenarios cannot close the performance question.

statistics.interpretation: post/main directly measures the final cumulative branch including new parsed-question reuse and upstream-only rule ordering. No individual optimization is causally isolated. Both prior full long-window observations remain unchanged; this is new code, not repeated selection of the same artifact.
statistics.UDP: Two main/post pairs in opposite order only; report both ratios and counts without inferential CI. The cumulative DNS lookup changes affect UDP too, so this is a guard, not a renewed broad performance-equivalence claim.
statistics.exclusion: No retries, W filter, direction unanimity requirement, removal or replacement. All invalid observations remain; invalid/incomplete comparisons cannot close the cost question.
statistics.DHCP: Not rerun: The new changes are DNS lookup changes. Earlier long DHCP evidence remains scoped to its tested workload; no zero-regression claim.

secondary_analysis.scope: Post-run read-only secondary analysis of retained final parsed/main windows; no new load
limits: /proc/stat is sampled within epochs and omits subsecond edge gaps; low steal does not prove causality.
cgroup total is primary; user/system decomposition alone does not identify function or syscall cause.
No samples/windows removed or repeated. Group median is distinct from median paired ratio.

interpretation.final_TCP: Geometric mean ratio0.97391766 (-2.6082%), paired-log 95% interval[0.88717200,1.06914511] (-11.2828% to +6.9145%). Neither CPU increase nor decrease is confirmed for this final artifact. The interval does not prove equality or zero regression and retains possible small cost increase; the per-scenario upper bound is +6.91%.
interpretation.pair_direction: Four of six pairs decrease and two increase. Paired median ratio0.98063878; AB median0.97341586 versus BA1.05586653 conflict in direction. Do not claim variation was proven to be pure noise.
interpretation.absolute_CPU: Mean main38.487283 versus final37.325222 us/query, mean paired delta-1.162061. Separate run medians37.354175 versus37.453450 differ from the paired-ratio median; both are retained.
interpretation.CPU_split: Mean user5.802475→11.222856 and system32.684806→26.102367 us/query. cgroup total remains primary; this variable accounting split is not evidence for a function/syscall cause.
interpretation.UDP_guard: Opposite-order post/main ratios1.01463634 (+1.4636%) and0.94125935 (-5.8741%). Both behavior-valid; no inferential interval was planned or calculated, and two descriptive pairs cannot establish equivalence or absence of regression.
interpretation.prior_observations: The original36-window result and subsequent22-window main/pre/post result remain complete and unchanged, including their confirmed TCP costs on earlier code. This final experiment does not retroactively reclassify those results or isolate each cleanup causally.
interpretation.host: No cgroup throttling; all ten-second idle CPU observations zero. CPU0 steal maximum0.01720%, any-core maximum0.07574%; boundary capture lag maximum4.931931ms and p95 send lag maximum86.388us. These facts do not prove causality.
interpretation.integrity: All16 windows retained with no retries, removal or substitutions. All methodology/behavior checks passed; no warmup/measurement wrong, timeout, transport error or skipped send. No concurrent tracing/build/test load; no idle CPU subtraction.

limits: Six pairs and one marginal per-scenario confidence interval, conditional on the stated paired-log model.
AB/BA subgroup difference and the interval crossing one leave uncertainty; no statistical equivalence or zero-regression assertion.
Main is static ET_EXEC and final is static PIE; cumulative source changes are compared, not individual optimization causes.
Final UDP guard has only two descriptive pairs. Earlier UDP/DHCP full measurements retain their original artifact identities and cannot prove every final workload has zero regression.
No physical-router, throughput ceiling, multirate scan, long-term leak or full replacement-performance qualification.
